templates_considered: requests_have_timeout (SEC-013): fits the timeout part; used as the base, but its statement.param_bound rule passes an omitted timeout, so a param_required rule was added
external_calls_handle_errors (LOG-010): fits the error-handling part; used as base; containment only checks try presence, not catch handling
tls_verification_on (SEC-011): does not fit; not in the ask
no_pii_in_responses, no_sensitive_data_in_logs, others: do not fit the ask

rules.covers: timeout is at most 30 seconds (from template)
timeout must be set explicitly ('a timeout set'); added beyond template
external call sits inside a try block (some error handling); catch contents not covered

ask_parts_not_covered.part: what the catch branch does with the failure (error handling beyond a try block)
external calls via ai.external.mcp.* and db.external.*.direct_query
ask_parts_not_covered.why: no check exists; these statements take no timeout and the containment rule was not extended to them because I did not confirm the exact names to list

ask_parts_not_covered.part: whether 30 seconds is the right timeout per vendor and whether a vendor outage falls back cleanly

assumptions: The hang came from outbound api.request calls with no timeout, so api.request is the main target; stream.from_request and webflow.request were included because the template lists them
A 30-second ceiling is acceptable; the template's limit was kept rather than a customer-specific number
Template severity (medium) and advisory enforcement are acceptable for a first version
No tags were added; the template has none and the ask did not name any
workspace_names_used: api.request statements in function acme_get_tracking, acme_sync_shipping_rates, acme_notify_sms, task retry_failed_webhooks, ai tool issue_refund, queries shipments/quote, payments/fraud_check, payments/charge, bank-accounts/link
env vars SHIPFAST_API_KEY, STRIPE_SECRET_KEY, PLAID_CLIENT_ID, PLAID_SECRET (seen only in the workspace, not in policy text)
confusions: The SEC-013 template's fill is '_nothing_', but its param_bound rule accepts an omitted timeout (judged at the 10s default). For a 'timeout must be set' ask the template alone does not satisfy it, and the skill does not say so. I had to find param_required in the catalogue myself.
param_required treats timeout = 10 as not set (per the catalogue description), which is surprising and only documented in the check description, not in the skill or template.

LOG-010's template summary says 'handle their own failures', but statement.containment only checks the try block exists. The summary oversells the check; the skill's Honesty guidance on this is not reflected in the template text.

LOG-010's limits say to add db.external.*.direct_query and ai.external.mcp.* statements to cover every outbound call, but the skill says statement names must be exact and gives no list of exact names for those, so I could not write them confidently.

The rule for 'no timeout' in an api.request is set via the `timeout` param, but the skill does not mention that a default-valued timeout is dropped on pull; I found this only in the param_required description.
Whether a single policy or two policies is right for 'timeout and error handling' was not addressed; each template has its own key, so I used two files.

The skill says 'Write a new policy active = true + advisory', which I followed; it also says never to run xano policy evaluate unless the user asks, which I did not run, so there are no real findings to report.
wished_for: A template or recipe for 'every outbound call has a timeout and a try block' that combines both rules, with the exact list of outbound statement names including db.external and ai.external variants
A note in the template or skill that the timeout template's rule accepts an omitted timeout, and that param_required is needed for a 'set' requirement
An example of a timeout value that is not 10 for the explicit-set rule
why_confidence: Both files parse with exit 0 and no warnings, and the checks match the timeout and try-block parts of the ask. Confidence is not high because the catch contents and the MCP/db.external calls are not covered, and no evaluate run was done to confirm which workspace objects are flagged; the object list is a prediction from reading the files.
